S  directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  C482 No.2094 of 2023  Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Ms. Mamta Arya, Advocate, holding brief of Mrs. Prabha Naithani, Advocate, for the applicant.
Mr. S.C. Dhumka, AGA, for the State of Uttarakhand.

This C482 application puts a challenge to the proceedings of the Criminal Case No.49 of 2023,
"State Vs. Uday Raj Singh", being the proceedings on which the cognizance have been taken for the offence under section 420 of IPC.
Learned counsel for the applicant argues that it is purely a civil dispute, hence, a criminal cognizance should not have been taken and in all probability the reliance has been placed on the judgment of "Bhajan lal", as rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court but with the changed legal scenario, the Hon'ble Apex Court has taken a converse view by Bench of equal strength that the civil offences too may have an element of criminality, which is required to be tested by the trial court.

The same principles has been laid down in the judgment of 2021 SCC online Supreme Court, 976,
"Mitesh Kumar J. Sha Versus The State of Karnataka & Ors" .

sentences.text: Since the offence relates to section 420 of IPC, it will be amenable to the jurisdiction of "Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another" as reported in 2022 (10) SCC 51, this C482 application would stand disposed of in terms of the said judgment.
